effects.prompt: Remove a suspense counter from an aura you control to give this +2{d} this chain link?

_comment: 'When this defends, you may remove a suspense counter from an aura you control. If you do, this gets +2{d} this chain link.' Shape copied from shipped evo/infuse_alloy_yellow.json, which implements Galvanize - the same 'when this defends, you may <pay>; if you do, +2{d}' sentence - as TRIGGERED ON_DEFEND -> MAY -> [cost, MODIFY_DEFENSE_VALUE]. Declining runs nothing, so 'if you do' needs no plumbing (release note: optional effect, chosen at resolution; no priority between the effects - one atomic MAY block). The +2 is MODIFY_DEFENSE_VALUE (moves combat.defense_mods), not MODIFY_ATTACK-style per-card defense: the damage-step recalc RESETS each defender to printed {d} before re-applying mods (engine._recalculate_total_defense), so a naive per-card bump written at defend time is wiped before damage; defense_mods survive because recalc re-applies them, and CombatState is rebuilt per attack, which IS 'this chain link' scope. Since this equipment is a declared defender whenever its ON_DEFEND trigger fires, +2 to the defending total == this gets +2{d} for the link. Counter removal targets an aura via REMOVE_COUNTERS' object-target compiler (zone ARENA == permanents, which includes the auras SubZoneView); filter CARD_IS_TYPE Aura + HAS_COUNTER suspense, and the controller picks among several (_ask_player). The +2 sub-effect carries its own REF_EXISTS gate on record_as 'suspense_removed', so if the player accepts but no qualifying aura exists, the empty pool sets no ref and no +2 lands - the 'if you do' holds even in the degenerate case. KNOWN IMPRECISION, flagged: the MAY's outer gate is CONTROLS_SUBTYPE Aura, because no condition combines 'aura you control' WITH a counter test (CARD_IN_ZONE has cost/type/color/power/class/keyword/name filters but none for counters). So the prompt can be offered when you control an aura that has no suspense counter; declining is free and accepting then grants nothing (see REF_EXISTS above), so behaviour is correct - only the prompt is occasionally spurious. counter_type 'suspense' copied from the producer, aps/pleiades.json. Printed BladeBreak keyword fires from the card DB keywords field; deliberately NOT authored here (re-authoring a printed keyword is a defect). No known gaps.
